def-qa-18-marked-set-and-stationary-mass:
## Definition

Let $(X,P,\pi)$ be a finite reversible Markov chain with positive stationary law, as in [[def-qa-17-finite-reversible-chain]], and let $\mathcal M\subseteq X$ be a set of marked states. Its **stationary marked mass** is

$$\varepsilon:=\pi(\mathcal M)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal M}\pi_x.$$

For a specified threshold $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1]$, the **marked-set detection promise problem** has yes-instances with $\mathcal M\ne\varnothing$ and $\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon_0$, and no-instances with $\mathcal M=\varnothing$. The required classical output is one bit distinguishing these two cases; its permitted failure probability is a separate algorithm input. In the uniform-chain case, $\pi_x=1/|X|$, so $\varepsilon=|\mathcal M|/|X|$.

The **marked-state finding promise problem** has inputs with $\varepsilon\ge\varepsilon_0$ and requires a classical output $x\in\mathcal M$. It is a different output relation from detection. A claimed output is checked by the declared finite projective measurement and marked predicate; the corresponding outcome law is [[def-qc-projective-measurement]] and [[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]]. The encoding of $X$, the coherent marked predicate, and all state-preparation and transition circuits are supplied input data, not consequences of the finite chain matrix.
def-qa-18-classical-hitting-time:
## Definition

Let $X$ be the finite state set, $P$ its row-transition matrix, $\mathcal M\subseteq X$ the marked set, $U=X\setminus\mathcal M$, and $P_{UU}$ the principal submatrix indexed by $U$. For an initial probability row vector $\mu$, the **hitting-time survival law** is

$$\Pr_\mu(\tau_{\mathcal M}>t):=\mu_U P_{UU}^{\,t}\mathbf 1_U,\qquad t\in\mathbb N_0,$$

where $\mu_U$ is the restriction of $\mu$ to $U$ and $\mathbf 1_U$ is the all-ones column vector on $U$. This is the finite sum of probabilities of all length-$t$ paths that remain in $U$; it does not require a path-space construction. For $U=\varnothing$ the right side is $0$; for $\mathcal M=\varnothing$ it is $1$.

The hitting time $\tau_{\mathcal M}:=\inf\{t\ge0:X_t\in\mathcal M\}$ is the $\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$-valued variable determined by this survival law. Its extended expectation is $\mathbb E_\mu\tau_{\mathcal M}=\sum_{t\ge0}\Pr_\mu(\tau_{\mathcal M}>t)$, and a constant-success hitting bound is a specified integer $t$ for which $\Pr_\mu(\tau_{\mathcal M}\le t)$ is bounded below by a positive constant. These resource conventions are kept separate.
lem-qa-18-absorbing-walk-discriminant-de:
## Statement

Let $P$ be a finite symmetric row-stochastic matrix on $X$, and let $\mathcal M\subseteq X$, $U=X\setminus\mathcal M$. Define the row-stochastic absorbing matrix

$$P'_{xy}=\begin{cases}1,&x=y\in\mathcal M,\\0,&x\in\mathcal M,\ y\ne x,\\P_{xy},&x\in U.\end{cases}$$

For the general row-stochastic discriminant $D(P')_{xy}=\sqrt{P'_{xy}P'_{yx}}$ of [[def-qa-17-szegedy-transition-isometry]],

$$D(P')=P_{UU}\oplus I_{\mathcal M},$$

where $P_{UU}$ is the principal submatrix on $U$. In general $P'$ need not be symmetric or reversible.
lem-qa-18-symmetric-compressed-walk-boun:
## Statement

Let $X$ be a finite set of size $n\ge2$, and let $P=(I+Q)/2$ where $Q$ is a symmetric row-stochastic matrix. Let $\mathbf u=n^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_X$. Assume the second-largest eigenvalue of $P$ is at most $1-\delta$, where $0<\delta\le1$. For $\mathcal M\subseteq X$, put $\varepsilon=|\mathcal M|/n$, $U=X\setminus\mathcal M$, and let $\Pi_U$ be the coordinate orthogonal projection defined by $\Pi_Ue_x=e_x$ for $x\in U$ and $\Pi_Ue_x=0$ for $x\notin U$. Let $P_U=\Pi_UP\Pi_U$ restricted to vectors supported on $U$. Then $P$ has spectrum in $[0,1]$ and

$$\|P_U\|\le 1-\delta\varepsilon.$$

The empty compression has norm $0$ by convention.
thm-qa-18-classical-spectral-hitting-bou:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[lem-qa-18-symmetric-compressed-walk-bound]], suppose $\varnothing\ne\mathcal M\ne X$ and start uniformly on $U=X\setminus\mathcal M$. Then

$$\Pr(\tau_{\mathcal M}>t)\le(1-\delta\varepsilon)^t\qquad(t\in\mathbb N_0),$$

so $\mathbb E\tau_{\mathcal M}\le1/(\delta\varepsilon)$ and $O(1/(\delta\varepsilon))$ steps give constant success probability. If $\mathcal M=X$, the hitting time is $0$.
def-qa-18-random-access-gate-model:
## Definition

Let a QRAM contain an ordered classical memory word $z=(z_0,\ldots,z_{L-1})\in\{0,1\}^L$, with $L\ge1$. Its **random-access quantum-memory gate** acts on an address register encoding $i\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, a target bit $b$, and the memory register by

$$|i,b,z_0\cdots z_{L-1}\rangle\longmapsto |i,z_i,z_0\cdots z_{i-1}b z_{i+1}\cdots z_{L-1}\rangle.$$

For address superpositions, this basis action is extended linearly. On valid addresses it swaps the target with the addressed memory bit, so the gate is an involutive permutation of the ordered computational basis and hence unitary; unused address encodings, if any, are fixed. One call has cost one QRAM gate-time unit by this model's convention. A read into a clean scratch target followed by copying and restoring the addressed bit uses the corresponding additional calls. The memory word itself, its address width, the circuit used to construct or update it, and the other ordinary gates are separate charged resources. This is a quantum random-access memory model; it does not assert an implementation by a bounded-arity ordinary circuit of the same gate count.
alg-qa-18-reversible-walk-finding:
## Definition

This is the finite-generation and execution procedure OP2 in `research/quantum-algorithms-planning/operational-contracts.md`, section “OP2 — MNRS approximate reflection and finite tolerant recursive finding”, transcribed with its declared constants and charged branches.

**Input.** A finite ergodic reversible row chain $(X,P,\pi)$ with $\pi_x>0$, a lower absolute-gap bound $\delta_0>0$, a coherent marked predicate with promise $\pi(\mathcal M)=0$ or $\pi(\mathcal M)\ge\varepsilon_0>0$, a charged stationary walk-state preparation $A_\pi$ of cost $S$, row/update circuits with their inverse and controlled access implementing $W=U^2$ at cost $U$, a coherent marked-bit check at cost $C$, and a failure target $\rho\in(0,1)$. The matrix $P$ alone supplies no state preparation or transition circuit.

**Approximate stationary reflection $R(\beta)$.** Set $\Delta_0=2\sqrt{\delta_0}$, $s=\lceil\log_2(4\pi/\Delta_0)\rceil$, and $k=\max(1,\lceil\log_2(2/\beta)\rceil)$, using certified interval arithmetic for real constants and ceilings. Append $k$ separate $s$-bit zero phase registers. Coherently execute QA07 phase estimation on $W$ in each register, constructing controlled powers from the declared controlled $W$ access. If at least one phase register is nonzero, apply $-I$ to the walk state. If all are zero, apply the exact row-space reflection $R_A=2TT^*-I$ using the charged row-preparation, inverse, and zero-state reflection calls. Reverse the $k$ phase-estimation circuits in reverse chronological order. Charge $2k(2^s-1)$ controlled walk/inverse constituent calls, the controlled $R_A$ branch, all-zero comparisons, phase-register gates, and the allocated classical arithmetic. The all-zero branch is required: $W$ has the extra zero-phase subspace $A^\perp\cap B^\perp$, where $R_A=-I$, while $R_A=+I$ on the stationary state.

**Recursive circuit $A_i$.** Let $\gamma=1/120$, $\beta_i=18\gamma/(4\pi^3i^2)$ for $i\ge1$, and $A_0=I$. For $i>0$, allocate a fresh $K_i$ for $R(\beta_i)$ and execute chronologically: (i) $A_{i-1}$, the marked phase flip, and $A_{i-1}^\dagger$; (ii) coherently test every older $K_j$, $j<i$, applying $-I$ if any is nonzero and otherwise applying $R(\beta_i)$ on the walk and fresh $K_i$; compute and uncompute the control predicate; (iii) apply $A_{i-1}$. An inverse means the exact reversed finite gate list, not a reset of measured work.

**Tolerant finding wrapper.** If $\varepsilon_0\ge1/2$, take $n_s=\lceil\ln(1/\rho)/\ln2\rceil$ fresh stationary samples, verify each label, return the first marked label, and output `NO MARKED` if all fail. Otherwise, let $t_{\max}$ be the least integer $t\ge0$ such that $3^t\arcsin\sqrt{\varepsilon_0}\ge\pi/4$. Determine it by certified interval comparison or the exact-algebraic threshold test; equality takes the $\ge$ branch. Let $n_{\rm out}=\lceil20\ln(1/\rho)\rceil+20$. In each outer trial:

1. Prepare a fresh stationary sample, test its first label, and return it if marked.
2. Prepare a fresh stationary walk state with all $K_1,\ldots,K_{t_{\max}}$ zero.
3. For $i=1,\ldots,t_{\max}$, apply $A_i$, measure marked/unmarked, and on a marked outcome verify and return the label. On an unmarked outcome retain the conditional current state and all auxiliary registers, and continue; do not reprepare or reset them.
4. If no level succeeds, discard the trial and begin the next fresh outer trial.

If all trials fail, output `NO MARKED`. Every loop has a finite cap; all confidence calculations, comparisons, reversible predicates, retained auxiliary space, state preparation, update, inverse, controlled, reflection, and check costs are charged. In the $\varepsilon_0\ge1/2$ branch, the cap above gives false-negative probability at most $\rho$; in the other branch correctness and the sharper cost are proved separately in [[thm-qa-18-reversible-search-cost]].
def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-w:
## Definition

Let $N\ge2$, let $\mathcal V$ be a finite nonempty value set, and let $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$, where $[N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}$. A **coherent value oracle** is a supplied finite unitary $O_f$ with an explicitly declared encoding and action $|i,z\rangle\mapsto|i,z\mathbin\oplus\operatorname{enc}(f(i))\rangle$ on valid addresses and target strings, as in [[def-qc-coherent-function-oracle]]. Oracle-query cost and ordinary gate-occurrence cost are separate coordinates under [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. The function table or name alone supplies no oracle circuit.

For $N\ge4$ and $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the **lazy Johnson walk** has state space $\Omega_r=\{S\subseteq[N]:|S|=r\}$ and transitions

$$P(S,S)=\tfrac12,\qquad P(S,S\setminus\{i\}\cup\{j\})=\frac{1}{2r(N-r)}\quad(i\in S,\ j\notin S),$$

with all other entries zero. Its marked vertices are

$$\mathcal M_f:=\{S\in\Omega_r:\exists i,j\in S,\ i\ne j,\ f(i)=f(j)\}.$$

The stored data at $S$ are the $r$ labeled values $(f(i))_{i\in S}$. Preparing the uniform $r$-subset state and loading these values has value-query cost $S_0=r$, with subset preparation gates charged separately. A neighbor update erases the removed value and loads the added value, so its value-query cost is $U_0=2$; the XOR oracle is its own inverse. Checking whether the stored subset is marked uses no further value queries, so $C_0=0$, but comparison gates and memory accesses are charged. After measuring a marked subset, scanning its stored values outputs a colliding pair with no additional value query; the scan's gate/time cost remains separate. For $N\le3$, use direct pairwise comparison rather than the $r$-subset walk. The lower bound $r\ge2$ is essential: a one-element subset cannot contain a collision pair.
def-qa-18-canonical-skip-list-for-elemen:
## Definition

Let $N\ge4096$, $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, and $f:[N]\to[M]$ with the value encoding in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]]. Put $H=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$, $d=C=16\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil$, $R=2^{\lceil\log_2r\rceil}$, and $q=2^H$, and assume $d\le N$. Choose $H+1$ independent uniform coefficient tuples in $\mathbb F_q^d$ and use them as coefficients of degree-at-most-$(d-1)$ polynomials $p_{-1},p_0,\ldots,p_{H-1}$ in the polynomial-basis representation of $\mathbb F_q$. For each $i\in[N]$, let $\mathsf{enc}(i)$ be the field element whose $H$-bit polynomial-basis coordinate string is the $H$-bit binary encoding of $i-1$; these elements are distinct. Let $h(i)$ be the integer represented by the low $\log_2R$ bits of $p_{-1}(\mathsf{enc}(i))$, and let $b_\ell(i)$ be the low bit of $p_\ell(\mathsf{enc}(i))$. The **height** of $i$ is the number of consecutive $1$ bits starting at $b_0(i)$, capped at $H$; equivalently, $\operatorname{height}(i)\ge\ell$ exactly when $b_0(i)=\cdots=b_{\ell-1}(i)=1$.

For a subset $S\in\binom{[N]}r$, the fixed memory word has $R$ hash buckets, each with $C$ slots, and one overflow bit. If no bucket exceeds capacity, every $i\in S$ is stored in bucket $h(i)$; occupied slots are sorted by index, and each record contains $i$, $f(i)$, and its skip-list fields. A node identifier is the input index $i$; resolving it means computing $h(i)$ and scanning that bucket. If any bucket would exceed capacity, set the overflow bit and put the same fixed sentinel in the data slots. Thus the represented word is a total, unique function of the subset and seed; the skip-list structure is valid exactly when the overflow bit is zero.

The storage also contains two **nested skip lists**, one in increasing index order and one in lexicographic order of $(f(i),i)$. Level $\ell$ of either list, for $0\le\ell\le H$, contains exactly the keys with height at least $\ell$; level $0$ contains all keys. Each forward pointer names a node identifier and stores its **span**, the difference between the source and target ranks in level $0$ (the head sentinel has rank $-1$). These spans support rank and select operations. The two lists, bucket positions, pointers, and spans are the unique ones determined by $(S,f|_S,p_{-1},p_0,\ldots,p_{H-1})$; they do not depend on the path used to reach $S$. A capped search inspects at most $D=2\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1$ forward entries at each level before raising an overrun flag. This definition specifies a finite representation and search convention; it does not assert a probability or cost bound.
lem-qa-18-johnson-walk-spectrum:
## Statement

Let $N\ge4$ and $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$. For the lazy Johnson transition matrix $P$ on the $r$-subsets of $[N]$ from [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], all eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, are

$$\lambda_j=1-\frac{j(N+1-j)}{2r(N-r)},\qquad 0\le j\le r,$$

with multiplicity $\binom Nj-\binom N{j-1}$, where $\binom N{-1}=0$. They are nonnegative, and the absolute spectral gap is

$$\delta(P)=1-\lambda_1=\frac{N}{2r(N-r)}.$$
thm-qa-18-reversible-search-cost:
## Statement

Let $(X,P,\pi)$ be a finite ergodic reversible chain with absolute spectral gap $\delta\in(0,1]$. Suppose the marked set is empty or has stationary mass at least $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$. Let $S_0$ be the cost of preparing the stationary walk state, $U_0$ a common upper bound for one controlled $W$ update (with inverse access) and the exact controlled row-space reflection $R_A$ used by the construction, and $C$ the cost of a coherent marked check. For $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, one outer trial of [[alg-qa-18-reversible-walk-finding]] has one-sided error, finds a marked state with a fixed positive probability when one exists, and uses

$$S_0+O\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\left(\frac{U_0}{\sqrt\delta}+C\right)\right).$$

in the corresponding query/update/check cost coordinates. The capped wrapper with failure target $\rho\in(0,1)$ uses $O((S_0+\varepsilon^{-1/2}(U_0/\sqrt\delta+C))(1+\ln(1/\rho)))$ in that profile. When $\varepsilon\ge1/2$, its direct-sampling branch uses $O(S_0(1+\ln(1/\rho)))$. For gate, width, precision, and bit-time coordinates, the phase-register gates, controlled reflection, comparisons, numerical generation, and retained workspace are charged separately.
alg-qa-18-szegedy-phase-detection:
## Definition

**Input.** A finite symmetric lazy row-stochastic matrix $P$ on nonempty $X$, with uniform stationary law and, when $|X|\ge2$, promised gap $\delta(P)=1-\lambda_2(P)\ge\delta_0$ for a rational $\delta_0\in(0,1]$; a marked predicate with promise $\mathcal M=\varnothing$ or $|\mathcal M|/|X|\ge\varepsilon_0$ for rational $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1]$; a failure target $\beta\in(0,1)$; a supplied circuit $A_{\rm unif}$ preparing $|s\rangle=|X|^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in X}|x\rangle$ with its cost; and a row-preparation access model for the absorbing chain $P'$ of [[lem-qa-18-absorbing-walk-discriminant-decomposition]], including the controlled and inverse access used below. If $|X|=1$, the procedure measures its sole label with the marked predicate and terminates exactly, without a gap parameter or walk. The marked check, preparation, controlled walk, inverse, gate, precision, and description-bit costs are separate declared inputs. A matrix alone supplies none of these circuits.

**Output.** `NONEMPTY` if a marked label is found or the phase test accepts; otherwise `EMPTY`. A found label is returned and checked against the supplied predicate.

**Instructions.**

1. If $|X|=1$, measure its only label, evaluate the supplied predicate and return the exact answer. Otherwise set $\gamma_0=\arccos(1-\delta_0\varepsilon_0)$, $m=\lceil\log_2(32\pi/\gamma_0)\rceil$, and $Q=2^m$. Compute ceilings and comparisons with the certified-interval/exact-comparison resources declared by the input cost model.
2. Set $k=\lceil\ln(1/\beta)/\ln6\rceil$. Repeat the following fresh-state run $k$ times, stopping early if `NONEMPTY` is returned.
3. Prepare $|s\rangle$ with $A_{\rm unif}$, apply the supplied row preparation $V_{P'}$ to obtain the two-register row state, and measure the first register with the projective marked/unmarked test. If its label $x$ is marked, output `NONEMPTY` and $x$ immediately. This branch handles $\mathcal M=X$ without conditioning on a zero-probability event.
4. On the unmarked branch, run $m$-bit [[alg-qa-quantum-phase-estimation]] on the one-reflection walk $U'=S(2T'T'^*-I)$, where $T'$ is the row-preparation map for $P'$. Use the supplied controlled powers if available; otherwise implement each controlled $U'^{2^j}$ by $2^j$ sequential controlled one-step $U'$ calls. No controlled inverse of $U'$ is used.
5. For the measured integer $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, compute $d(y)=\min(y/Q,1-y/Q)$ using charged rational arithmetic. Return `NONEMPTY` exactly when $d(y)>\gamma_0/(4\pi)$; equality takes the `EMPTY` branch. Charge the threshold comparison and all phase-register/inverse-QFT gates.
6. If all $k$ fresh runs fail to return `NONEMPTY`, output `EMPTY`. A run uses one marked check, the supplied uniform-state and one row-preparation costs, one $m$-bit QPE, and its explicitly charged controlled-walk calls. With only one-step controlled access, QPE uses exactly $Q-1$ controlled $U'$ calls. Gate synthesis and classical coefficient/threshold bits are additional costs.
lem-qa-18-johnson-stored-data-query-acce:
## Statement

For the lazy Johnson chain and XOR value oracle in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], write $d_f(S)$ for the values at the indices of $S$, in increasing index order. In the pure value-query model, encoded vertex preparation costs $r$ queries. Coherent row preparation and its inverse, including controlled versions, cost at most two queries each. The corresponding controlled row-space reflection costs at most four queries, and a controlled $W=U^2$ step and its inverse cost at most eight. A stationary two-register walk state costs at most $r+2$ queries, and its marked check uses zero value queries. Gates, memory, uniform generation, and exact coefficient preparation are separate resources; no gate-time bound is asserted.
thm-qa-18-element-distinctness-query-cos:
## Statement

Let $N\ge4$, $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$ be given by the coherent value oracle in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], and suppose some distinct $a,b$ satisfy $f(a)=f(b)$. For any $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the lazy Johnson walk has absolute gap $\delta=N/[2r(N-r)]$, marked stationary mass at least $\varepsilon=r(r-1)/[N(N-1)]$, stored-vertex setup value-query cost $r$, elementary replacement-update cost $2$, and check cost $0$. The controlled row-access construction of [[lem-qa-18-johnson-stored-data-query-access]] supplies stationary edge-state setup at most $r+2$, controlled row reflection at most $4$, and controlled two-reflection walk/inverse at most $8$ value queries. The reversible-walk finding theorem therefore gives a constant-success marked-subset finder with

$$r+O\!\left(\frac{N}{\sqrt r}\right)$$

value queries. Taking $r=\min\{\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\max\{2,\lfloor N^{2/3}\rfloor\}\}$ gives $O(N^{2/3})$ queries. A measured marked subset contains a colliding pair among its stored values, which can be output without further value queries; comparison gates are separate resources.
thm-qa-18-detection-correctness-cost:
## Statement

Let $P=(I+Q)/2$ be a finite symmetric lazy transition matrix on a nonempty finite set $X$, with uniform stationary law. Fix $\delta_0\in(0,1]$; when $|X|\ge2$, suppose its second eigenvalue satisfies $\lambda_2(P)\le1-\delta_0$. For $|X|=1$, $\delta_0$ is an arbitrary parameter in this interval. Let the marked-set promise be $\mathcal M=\varnothing$ or $|\mathcal M|/|X|\ge\varepsilon_0$, where $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1]$. Give the algorithm the stated uniform-state circuit, a row-preparation access model for the absorbing chain $P'$, its controlled and inverse calls needed for the one-reflection walk, the marked check, and all their separate costs. Put

$$\gamma_0=\arccos(1-\delta_0\varepsilon_0),\quad m=\left\lceil\log_2\frac{32\pi}{\gamma_0}\right\rceil,\quad Q=2^m,\quad k=\left\lceil\frac{\ln(1/\beta)}{\ln6}\right\rceil,$$

for $\beta\in(0,1)$. Then [[alg-qa-18-szegedy-phase-detection]] has no false positive on an empty marked set and outputs `NONEMPTY` with probability at least $1-\beta$ on every promised nonempty instance. For $|X|\ge2$, let $C_{\rm init}=C_{\rm unif}+C_{\rm row}$, where the terms are the supplied uniform-state and one row-preparation costs, $C_{\rm mark}$ the initial marked check, $C_{\rm walk}$ the cost of one controlled one-reflection walk call, and $G_{\rm QPE}(m)$ the phase-register preparation and inverse-QFT gate cost. Its worst-case charged cost is at most

$$k\bigl(C_{\rm init}+C_{\rm mark}+(Q-1)C_{\rm walk}+G_{\rm QPE}(m)\bigr),$$

when only one-step controlled-walk access is supplied. The factorwise implementation of $C_{\rm walk}$ charges one controlled row-preparation inverse, one controlled row preparation, the controlled clean-state reflection, and the controlled swap. With separately supplied controlled powers, replace $(Q-1)C_{\rm walk}$ by the sum of their $m$ declared costs. This is a detection result; a `NONEMPTY` phase-test outcome does not supply a marked label. Synthesis, comparison arithmetic, description bits and precision remain separate coordinates.
thm-qa-18-element-distinctness-qr-access:
## Statement

Fix an encoding of values in $[M]$ by $b=O(\log(M+1))$ bits and take the parameter $r$ from [[thm-qa-18-element-distinctness-query-cost]]. For $N\ge4096$, the finite canonical storage of [[def-qa-18-canonical-skip-list-for-element-distinctness]] has hash-table lookup, rank/select, complement-unranking, value insertion/deletion, and collision-check subroutines with $\operatorname{polylog}(N+M)$ QRAM gate-time when their bounded searches do not overrun; the table uses $O(N^{2/3}\log^3(N+M))$ memory bits. A fixed threshold $N_0\ge4096$ is chosen below; the search uses this storage for $N\ge N_0$ and direct value comparison for the finite range $4\le N<N_0$.

For $N\ge N_0$, let $G_{\rm subset}$ be the gate-time of the supplied uniform $r$-subset preparation. Assume an explicit compatible realization of the controlled/inverse Johnson-walk access used by reversible finding exists on this canonical storage, uses the local operations proved below, and preserves the hash seed. Let $G_{\rm row}$ be the maximum gate-time of one charged walk-update unit in that realization, including the forward, inverse, controlled, reflection, and swap capabilities supplied for the lazy Johnson walk in [[def-qa-17-walk-access-model]] and any encoding conversion. Under this explicit interface assumption, the complete search has value-query cost $O(N^{2/3})$ and gate-time

$$G_{\rm subset}+O\!\left(r\operatorname{polylog}(N+M)+N^{2/3}\bigl(G_{\rm row}+\operatorname{polylog}(N+M)\bigr)\right).$$

The local storage operations are proved below; this item does not construct the compatible full row-access circuit or derive polylogarithmic bounds for $G_{\rm subset}$ and $G_{\rm row}$. The unconditional $O(N^{2/3}\operatorname{polylog}(N+M))$ gate-time conclusion requires $G_{\rm subset}=O(N^{2/3}\operatorname{polylog}(N+M))$ and $G_{\rm row}=O(\operatorname{polylog}(N+M))$.

The phase-estimation part of this gate-time profile uses the ideal continuous-rotation submodel of [[thm-qa-phase-estimation-access-cost]], where each exact controlled phase is one gate occurrence. Any synthesis overhead for a fixed finite gate alphabet is a separate cost.

For a Boolean value circuit with $G$ non-input gates, $E$ input-port uses, $D$ explicit layers, maximum per-wire layer fanout $F$, and $m$ output bits, one reversible XOR value query uses at most $6G+4E+m$ ordinary gate occurrences and has the explicit schedule depth

$$2D\bigl(2\lceil\log_2(F+1)\rceil+3\bigr)+2\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil+1.$$

This is the written depth of the supplied schedule under [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. It does not claim minimum-layer depth or include the other ordinary gates used by the walk data structure.
